title: SOC2 hypotheses and evidence lockbox (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, messy working notes for control hypotheses + evidence locations. Not polished — for Rafa + Trust squad to iterate. Use to seed interviews and evidence collection.

Context / scope:
- Focus: Common SOC2 trust criteria relevant to Redwood Inference: CC1 (control environment), CC2 (communication), CC3 (risk assessment), CC4 (control activities), CC5 (monitoring).
- Immediate sprint: inventory evidence for access controls, change control, incident response, and vendor management.
- Goal: have interview targets + evidence list by 2026-03-12 so we can triage gaps and assign owners.

High-level hypotheses (rough):
1) Access control: We rely on Okta + Google SSO for primary auth; privileged access is in a small admin group but there are 3 legacy service accounts with wide access that may not be on the official list. Evidence to find: Okta group membership export, admin onboarding/offboarding runbook, service account list from infra repo.
2) Change management: Releases go through GH PRs and have approvals, but some infra changes are done via CI templates and not always associated with PRs (infra: terraform in mono-repo). Evidence: PR history, release tags, CI run logs, terraform-state change logs.
3) Logging & monitoring: We forward most application logs to Splunk/Datadog; retention policy ambiguous for audit logs (some logs retained <90d). Evidence: logging retention policy docs, Splunk index configs, SRE playbook.
4) Incident response: There is a runbook but playbook maturity varies by team; major incidents have postmortems but small incidents sometimes only Slack notes. Evidence: postmortem folder, pager duty incident list, N-1 small incident threads in #ops-incidents.
5) Third party vendor mgmt: We have KMS/HSM provider, cloud provider contract, and a couple of data processor agreements — need central list and evidence of vendor risk evaluation. Evidence: legal contract summaries, vendor registry spreadsheet.

Control mapping (draft, map to likely evidence):
- Control: Logical access provisioning (CC6) -> Evidence: Okta SCIM provisioning logs, onboarding ticket in Linear, IAM policies in infra repo, quarterly access review emails.
- Control: Privileged access review -> Evidence: admin group membership exports (csv), meeting notes for review, any signed attestations.
- Control: Change approvals -> Evidence: GitHub PR approvals, CODEOWNERS coverage, CI run success + merge timestamps, change advisory calendar entry.
- Control: Segregation of duties -> Evidence: role definitions in HR doc, enforcement via GitHub branch protection + PR reviewers.
- Control: Backup & restore -> Evidence: backup job configs (S3 lifecycle), restore test logs, runbook.
- Control: Incident handling -> Evidence: incident playbook, pagerduty incidents, postmortem docs, timeline exports.

Evidence quick-checklist (what I can grab this week):
- Okta: export groups + SCIM provisioning logs (owner: @arielle).
- GitHub: PR review history for main infra repos (owner: @samir).
- CI: build logs for last 90 days for infra pipelines (owner: infra-runner alias).
- Logging configs: Splunk index retention, Datadog logs ingestion (owner: Lina).
- Postmortems: /shared/postmortems/ (search keywords: SOC2, incident) (owner: Rafael).
- Vendor registry: legal share -> trust-ops copy (owner: legal-trust).

Open questions / unknowns: (callouts to triage)
- Q1: Which service accounts are used for production migrations and who owns them? (possible orphaned accounts)
- Q2: Are there any ad-hoc one-off scripts that run with elevated keys from a developer laptop? Need to interview solutions engineers.
- Q3: Retention length for auth logs vs. application logs — is 90 days baseline across all indices? Compliance may require 1 year for audit trails.
- Q4: Evidence of access revocation process: is there an automated connector from HR offboarding -> Okta deprovisioning? If manual, need logs showing timeliness.

Interview plan (names + approximate questions):
- Arielle (identity): export groups, describe deprovision flow, show recent quarterly review notes.
- Samir (platform infra): explain infra change workflow, list exceptions, point to infra PRs that bypass CODEOWNERS.
- Lina (observability): confirm log retention for audit logs, provide config screenshots, clarify archived vs hot retention.
- Dev leads (solutions eng): list any scripted ops that bypass standard pipelines.
- Legal / procurement: vendor registry + dataprocessor agreements (contract dates, DPIA if available).

Short-term remediation/next steps (this sprint):
- Task 1: Run Okta group export + highlight any admin groups with >3 members. (owner: Arielle, due: 2026-03-09)
- Task 2: Pull GH PRs for infra repos last 6 months and flag merges without 2 reviewers. (owner: Samir, due: 2026-03-11)
- Task 3: Confirm log retention table and surface indices under 90d. (owner: Lina, due: 2026-03-10)
- Task 4: Create temporary evidence binder in /trust/evidence/sprint-03-2026 and start uploading artifacts as we find them. (owner: Rafael, due: 2026-03-12)

Artifacts / filenames I expect to create or collect:
- okta-groups-export-2026-03-08.csv
- infra-pr-review-gap-2026-03-11.csv
- splunk-index-retention-2026-03-09.txt
- incident-postmortem-index-2025-2026.md
- vendor-registry-trustcopy-2026-03.xlsx

Notes to self (tiny scribbles):
- keep momentum: 1 evidence item per day from each owner -> helps argue progress to auditors.
- don't over-index on perfect docs now — capture raw screenshots + logs, we can formalize later.
- flag any PII in artifacts before sharing in trust binder (mask emails/IDs).

Slack seeds / messages to send (drafts):
- @arielle-parker: quick ask — can you drop an Okta group membership export into /trust/tmp by EOD Tue? looking for admin groups + SCIM history.
- @samir-bose: ping for infra PR audit: can you run a grep for merged PRs without 2 approvals last 6mo?

Risks I care about:
- Orphaned privileged keys (high)
- Inconsistent change control across infra vs app (medium)
- Short audit log retention (medium-high)
- Fragmented vendor risk evidence (low-med)

If auditor asks for everything now: prioritize these artifacts: Okta group export, PR approvals, incident postmortems, log retention config, vendor list.

End-of-note: this is a working scratchpad. I'll re-run and clean into a formal evidence index once the binder has 10+ items. For now — collect and drop raw files under /trust/tmp and tag in the binder index.

Rafael
2026-03-05
